B3.1.procedure: Run cargo test --workspace --locked --lib -- --include-ignored --test-threads=1 --nocapture with disposable PostgreSQL 16. Rehearse an upload after service restart in the Chromium/Compose release.
B3.1.observed: Four fixture originals matched their manifests. The Chromium upload resumed at 1151 bytes and produced one asset and original. Missing and changed parts stayed unpublished. The journal linked the asset after finalization.

B3.2.procedure: Run npm --prefix web run test:photos against the Compose release with a fresh disposable PostgreSQL 16 database and private filesystem storage.
B3.2.observed: Separate guardian and learner sessions used the keyboard to upload, resume at 1151 bytes, match, unmatch and relink. One original retained its uploader and digest, duplicate requests made one link, and guardian attachment to a synthetic diary row returned 404.

B3.3.procedure: Run npm --prefix web run test:archive against the disposable Compose release.
B3.3.observed: Four ordered private originals downloaded with external requests blocked. The fifth stayed link-only until its supplied recording resumed at byte 4195170 and verified. One backing original retained its hash and both withdrawal paths were reversible. Guest and outsider requests for private originals returned scoped 404s; the selected-photo guest grant belongs to B5.

T3.procedure: Run npm --prefix web run test:photos, the photo-match adapter, and npm --prefix web run test:archive against the disposable Compose release.
T3.observed: Words-first and photo-first matching kept an independent original and its uploader. Four local attachments downloaded with external requests blocked. The fifth retained its position and link identity and gained one verified copy after a halfway interruption and resume.

photo-match.procedure: Run python3 tools/run_cases.py --case photo-match --timeout 60 -- node web/tests/photos.mjs --case against the Compose release.
photo-match.observed: The final B3.3 release reproduced one new original, one active match before unmatch, zero afterward, the guardian uploader and the original SHA-256.
